header.title: Ripple
header.description: A wave that expands from the pointer, like Material's ink effect. Each wave grows until it covers the whole host and fades out. `variant` sets the look (`ink`, `ring`, `pulse`), `trigger` when it appears (`click`, `hover` or `press`) and `origin` where it starts (`pointer` or `center`). The layer has `pointer-events: none`, so the child keeps receiving clicks.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Combine the props and click, hover or hold on the card.
playground.label: Tap me

base.title: Basic ripple
base.description: With the defaults (`variant="ink"`, `trigger="click"`, `origin="pointer"`) each click spawns a disc that grows from the pointer for `600` ms. Waves stack: you can click several times in a row. With the keyboard, focus the button and press Enter or Space: the wave starts from the center.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: `ink` is a filled disc. `ring` is just the edge (`2px`). `pulse` spawns three rings from the same point, `18%` of `duration` apart; here with `duration={900}`.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: `pointer` starts where you clicked. `center` always starts in the middle of the host, wherever you tap.

image.title: Over an image
image.description: The wave works over any content. Here with `variant="pulse"`, white and `intensity="lg"` so it shows over the photo.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: `click` spawns a wave on press. `hover` spawns it when the pointer enters (from the edge you came in through). `press` repeats waves while you hold, every `45%` of `duration` (at least `180` ms), and they follow the pointer if you move it. While held, each new wave reads the current props: if `variant`, `duration` or `isPaused` change, the next waves follow. The cards have `tabIndex={0}` to try it with the keyboard: Enter or Space spawn a wave from the center with `click` and `press`, and with `hover` the wave starts from the center when focus enters with Tab.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: `color` is the wave color; it accepts any CSS color. `intensity` mixes it with transparent. Without `color`, it uses `currentColor`: the host's text color, so the wave matches the content on a light or dark button. Prefer tokens.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: `duration` is how long each wave takes to grow and fade, in milliseconds.

delay.title: Delay
delay.description: `delay` delays the start of each wave after the click. Useful to sync the wave with another animation.

intensity.title: Intensity
intensity.description: `intensity` is the wave opacity: `sm` (`35%`), `md` (`55%`) or `lg` (`80%`). It also accepts a number from `0` to `1`.

asChild.title: On an element (asChild)
asChild.description: With `asChild`, the effect mounts directly on the child (a `button` here), without adding a `div`. Useful in flex rows or grids where an extra node breaks the layout. Next to it, the same button without the effect: Tab through them and the focus ring shows in full on both, because the layer clips the waves, not the root. With a void element like `img` or `input`, it falls back to the wrapping `div`.

state.title: Pause and disabled
state.description: Here with `trigger="hover"`, `pulse` and `duration={2400}`: hover and turn on `isPaused` while the waves grow: they stay frozen on screen and finish on unpause. No new waves are created while paused. `isDisabled` stops creating waves and hides the current ones; the child stays interactive.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onRipple` fires when the first wave appears and `outRipple` when the last one ends, with the reason in `event.reason`. Rapid clicks count as a single phase. The button still works: the click reaches the child and the wave fires anyway. If you activate it with Enter or Space, the wave starts from the center.

header.title: Ripple API
header.description: Reference for the props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types of `Ripple`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples of each variant, trigger and option.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from `@gem-org/gemffects/ripple` with `ripple.css`, or from the package root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> (except color) and passes them to the root div (or the child, with asChild). onPointerDown, onPointerUp, onPointerCancel, onPointerEnter, onPointerLeave and onPointerMove run before the effect's internal logic, as do onClick, onKeyDown and onFocus before the keyboard logic. --gemfx-ripple-duration, -intensity and -color are written after style, but only when you pass duration, intensity or color.

items.decorative: The wave layer is decorative (aria-hidden, pointer-events: none): it doesn't change the child's semantics or interaction.
items.keyboard: With click and press, Enter or Space spawn a wave from the center: on the focused root (with asChild on a control, or with tabIndex) or when a nested control is activated by keyboard. Holding the key doesn't repeat it. With hover, when keyboard focus enters the host from outside, a wave starts from the center; it doesn't happen when focus moves between elements inside or with the focus a mouse click leaves.
items.focus: The root doesn't clip anything: the layer clips the waves (overflow: hidden, clip-path). The child's focus ring, or the element's own with asChild, shows in full even when it's drawn outside.
items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce no waves are created, and onRipple doesn't fire.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion (or the gemfx-ignore-reduced-motion class on an ancestor) keeps the waves. Use it only when essential.
items.touch: It doesn't block touch scrolling. disabledOnTouch ignores touches; mouse and pen still work.

items.root: Root. `inline-flex`, `position: relative` and `isolation: isolate`. It doesn't clip its content, so it doesn't cut the focus ring. Sets the variable defaults.
items.variant: Active variant. `ring` and `pulse` swap the fill for a `2px` inner edge (`box-shadow`).
items.trigger: Active trigger. Not added with `isDisabled` or `isActive={false}`. Has no styles of its own.
items.paused: Added with `isPaused`. Pauses the wave animation; the timer that removes them pauses too, so they stay on screen until unpaused.
items.inactive: Added with `isDisabled` or `isActive={false}`. Hides the waves (`display: none`).
items.touchDisabled: Added with `disabledOnTouch`. Has no styles of its own.
items.surface: Wraps the child (`z-index: 0`, `flex: 1 1 auto`). With `asChild`, the class goes on the child itself.
items.layer: Wave layer (`position: absolute`, `inset: 0`, `z-index: 1`, `pointer-events: none`, `aria-hidden`). Clips the waves to the host radius with `overflow: hidden`, `contain: paint`, `clip-path: inset(0)` and `border-radius: inherit`.
items.wave: Each wave. A circle centered on `--gemfx-ripple-x` / `-y` with the `gemfx-ripple-wave` animation (from `scale(0)` and opacity `1` to `scale(1)` and opacity `0`). `classNames.wave` goes on each one.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Root variables only go inline when you pass the matching prop; otherwise you can set them from a class. Wave variables are written inline on each wave and are for reading.

items.color: Wave color. Only inline when you pass `color`; otherwise it's `currentColor`.
items.timing: Animation duration and color-mix opacity. Inline only when you pass `duration` or `intensity`. `-duration` from CSS only changes the animation: each wave's removal and the `pulse` stagger use the `duration` prop, so pass it as a prop to change the timing.
items.wave: Position, diameter (what it takes to cover the host from the origin) and delay of each wave (`delay` plus the `pulse` stagger).

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global variables Ripple reads as defaults.

items.intensity: Default of `--gemfx-ripple-intensity` in the CSS (fallback `55%`). Overridden by the inline value when you pass `intensity`.

content.title: Content
content.description: What receives the wave and where the effect mounts.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Wave look, origin, color and intensity.

state.title: Trigger and state
state.description: When waves appear, how they pause and how they turn off.

items.asChild: Applies the effect to the single child, without a wrapping `div`. With void elements like `img` or `input`, it falls back to the wrapping `div`.
items.variant: `ink` is a filled disc, `ring` an edge and `pulse` three staggered rings.
items.origin: `pointer` starts at the event point and `center` in the middle of the host.
items.color: Wave color. Defaults to `currentColor` (the host's text color). Prefer tokens.
items.intensity: Wave opacity: `35%` / `55%` / `80%`, or a number from `0` to `1`.
items.trigger: `click` spawns a wave on press, `hover` on pointer enter and `press` repeats them while held. With `click` and `press`, Enter or Space spawn a wave from the center; with `hover`, keyboard focus entering the host does.
items.isActive: Allows new waves. When `false` it hides the current ones.
items.isPaused: Freezes the waves on screen (their timer too) and blocks new ones. They finish on unpause.
items.isDisabled: Creates no waves and hides the current ones; the child stays interactive.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Keeps the waves even if the user prefers less motion. Only when essential.
items.disabledOnTouch: Ignores the touch pointer; mouse and pen still work.
items.onRipple: Fires when the first wave appears.
items.outRipple: Fires when the last wave ends, or on disable or unmount.
items.style: Inline styles for the root. The effect variables are written after, only for the props you passed.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `div`, or the child with `asChild`).
